units.function: Embedded-Postgres route tests for a human user's Agent-inbox policy, self-service allowlisting, administrator overrides and same-company membership/Agent validation.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest/Express -> inbox policy routes -> real Drizzle/PostgreSQL membership, permission, Agent, policy and activity tables; authentication middleware and actual inbox actions are outside this unit.
units.keyDataModels: Human user/company membership, Agent, principal permission grant, open/allowlist/disabled inbox policy, allowed Agent IDs and policy-update activity.
units.lifecycle: Read implicit policy -> user or authorized administrator validates target/Agents -> persist policy -> append update audit -> later inbox routes consume the policy.
units.testAssessment: All 5 tests skipped in both sandboxed and approved unsandboxed runs due unavailable embedded PostgreSQL. The source covers basic ownership/admin/tenant validation but not policy consumption, concurrency, revocation, granular delegation or full identity paths.
units.designRationale: Let Agents safely tidy user inboxes with a simple user-controlled mode, while company permission administrators can support users and allowlists cannot reference another company's Agents.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must preserve human control of private work, approval and responsibility queues through explicit least-privilege delegation rather than assuming every company Agent may act until opted out.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as default-deny HumanWorkspaceDelegation/DataAuthorization: exact human principal, eligible Agent/Connector, allowed actions and object classes, purpose, expiry, revocation/version, accountable manager and optional approval. Administrator overrides require reason, step-up policy, user notification and immutable evidence; in-flight actions bind the policy version.
units.responsibilityConflict: The open default and coarse policy allow an unspecified population of Agents to affect a human inbox with no purpose, Work/Run, accountable human or action digest. An administrator can change another user's delegation without tested notice or consent evidence.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL insecure default: absent policy means open Agent access. CRITICAL granularity gap: read/archive/dismiss/approve/data-disclosure actions are not separately scoped. HIGH administrator-override gap: no reason, step-up, user notice or separation-of-duty test. HIGH lifecycle gap: no expiry, revocation/version or in-flight binding. HIGH Agent eligibility gap: active status, capability, manager and Connector health are untested. MEDIUM concurrency gap: no ETag/CAS. MEDIUM verification gap: all database tests skipped locally.
